title: Install State Department appointees while Senate confirmation is pending
proposal: The text recommends that the President place State Department nominees into their jobs before the Senate confirms them, to push the Senate to act faster.
quote: the next President can exert leverage on the Senate if he or she is willing to place State Department appointees directly into those roles, pending confirmation

title: Increase the number of political appointees at the State Department
proposal: The text recommends filling non-Senate-confirmed senior roles, such as deputy assistant secretaries, with political appointees and adding more political appointees overall.
quote: Given the department’s size, the next Administration should also increase the number of political appointees to manage it.

title: Replace State Department leadership on Inauguration Day
proposal: The text recommends that new senior appointees be chosen in advance and in place on day one, so that no one leading the department on the morning of January 20 still holds that role by day's end.
quote: No one in a leadership position on the morning of January 20 should hold that position at the end of the day.

title: Create training and mentorship for State Department political appointees
proposal: The text recommends that the Secretary of State hold regular strategy meetings and trainings for political appointees and set up a mentorship program pairing experienced and newer appointees.
quote: using them as the foundation for a mentorship program for less experienced political appointees

title: Accept all political ambassadors' resignations and review career ambassadors
proposal: The text recommends accepting the resignations of all politically appointed ambassadors at the start of the term and quickly reviewing every career ambassador.
quote: It should both accept the resignations of all political ambassadors and quickly review and reassess all career ambassadors.

title: Recall ambassadors seen as opposed to the new administration
proposal: The text recommends immediately recalling ambassadors in countries where U.S. policy will change a lot, and any who have shown hostility toward the new administration. It suggests close allies of the President for key posts.
quote: as well as any who have evinced hostility toward the incoming Administration or its agenda, should be recalled immediately.

title: Freeze State Department spending, aid, contracts and hiring pending review
proposal: The text recommends that on day one the Secretary of State freeze work on unratified agreements, foreign aid payments, contracts and hiring until political appointees review them.
quote: the Secretary of State should order an immediate freeze on all efforts to implement unratified treaties and international agreements, allocation of resources, foreign assistance disbursements

title: Freeze ongoing treaty and international agreement negotiations
proposal: The text recommends that the President tell the Secretary of State to pause all ongoing treaty and international agreement negotiations and check whether they fit the new foreign policy.
quote: He or she should direct the Secretary of State to freeze any ongoing treaty or

title: Stop enforcing treaties the Senate has not ratified
proposal: The text recommends ordering the State Department to stop enforcing any treaty the Senate has not ratified and to review how such enforcement affected the department.
quote: order an immediate stand-down on enforcement of any treaties that have not been ratified by the Senate

title: Send treaty-like 'agreements' to the Senate and pause compliance
proposal: The text recommends identifying international "agreements" that are really treaties, suspending U.S. compliance with them, and sending them to the Senate for approval.
quote: suspend compliance pending presidential transmittal of those agreements to the Senate for advice and consent
agency: State Department / DOJ / White House Counsel

title: Withdraw treaties pending before the Senate for 20+ years
proposal: The text recommends withdrawing treaties that have waited for Senate approval for 20 years or more, and updating the paperwork for any old treaty still worth ratifying.
quote: The next Administration should also move to withdraw from treaties that have been under Senate

title: Revoke most other agencies' authority to negotiate agreements (C-175)
proposal: The text recommends that the Secretary of State take back most "Circular 175" authorities that let other agencies negotiate international agreements.
quote: The Secretary of State must revoke most outstanding C-175 authorities that have been granted to other

title: Route State Department contact with Congress through political appointees
proposal: The text recommends that the department coordinate all congressional contact with the White House and that political appointees lead any approved engagement with Congress.
quote: All such authorized department engagements with Congress must be driven and handled by political appointees

title: Keep a central State Department office for China policy
proposal: The text recommends supporting the concept of the State Department's Office of China Coordination ("China House"), with changes, to centralize U.S. diplomatic efforts on China.
quote: Nonetheless, the concept is one a Republican Administration should support mutatis mutandis.

title: Strictly enforce visa reciprocity with all countries
proposal: The text recommends granting visas to a country's citizens only on terms that match how that country treats Americans, and updating these rules quickly when other countries change theirs.
quote: The United States should strictly enforce the doctrine of reciprocity when issuing visas to all foreign nationals.

title: Fully enforce visa sanctions on countries refusing deportees
proposal: The text recommends fully using the law (INA section 243(d)) to stop issuing some or all visas to countries that will not take back their citizens ordered removed from the U.S.
quote: Visa sanctions under section 243(d) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA),8 enacted into law to motivate countries to accept the return

title: Indefinitely reduce refugee admissions
proposal: The text recommends cutting the number of refugees admitted through the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for an indefinite time and shifting screening resources to the border.
quote: will necessitate an indefinite curtailment of the number of USRAP refugee admissions

title: Restart Remain in Mexico and safe third-country agreements
proposal: The text recommends bringing back the Remain in Mexico policy and safe third-country agreements on day one to address asylum seekers at the southern border.
quote: Reimplementation of the Remain in Mexico policy, safe third-country agreements, and other measures to address the influx of non-Mexican asylum applicants

title: Let DHS keep authority to negotiate security agreements
proposal: The text recommends that, as an exception to reining in other agencies, the Department of Homeland Security keep or regain authority to negotiate security agreements with other countries.
quote: the Department of Homeland Security should retain (or regain) C-175 authorities for negotiating bilateral and multilateral security agreements

title: Review the Diversity Visa, student and exchange visa programs
proposal: The text recommends that the State Department evaluate security-sensitive visa programs, including the Diversity Visa lottery and F (student) and J (exchange visitor) visas.
quote: Key programs include, but should not be limited to, the Diversity Visa program, the F (student) visa program, and J (exchange visitor) visa program.

title: Write an 'Article X' strategy document on China
proposal: The text recommends that the State Department and National Security Council draft a major strategy paper on China, modeled on George Kennan's Cold War "Article X."
quote: Along with the National Security Council, the State Department should draft an Article X, which should be a deeply philosophical look at the China challenge.

title: Russia-Ukraine view: continue military and economic aid to Ukraine
proposal: One view the text describes supports continued U.S. military and economic aid to Ukraine, and NATO and U.S. troops if needed, until Russia is defeated and pre-invasion borders return.
quote: This viewpoint argues for continued U.S. involvement including military aid, economic aid, and the presence of NATO and U.S. troops if necessary.
contested: First of three conservative viewpoints presented; the chapter does not choose among them.

title: Russia-Ukraine view: end U.S. involvement and seek a negotiated settlement
proposal: A second view the text describes says the U.S. should stop its involvement, leave Ukraine's defense to European nations, and seek a quick negotiated settlement.
quote: European nations directly affected by the conflict should aid in the defense of Ukraine, but the U.S. should not continue its involvement.
contested: Second of three conservative viewpoints presented; the chapter does not choose among them.

title: Russia-Ukraine view: limit aid to paid-for military aid only
proposal: A third view the text describes would allow continued U.S. support only if it is fully paid for, limited to military aid, and tied to a clear strategy that does not risk American lives.
quote: continued U.S. involvement must be fully paid for; limited to military aid (while European allies address Ukraine’s economic needs)
contested: Third of three conservative viewpoints presented; the chapter does not choose among them.

title: Adopt a 'sovereign Mexico' policy against cartels
proposal: The text recommends a policy calling for Mexico to regain full control of its territory from criminal cartels and taking all available steps to support that quickly.
quote: The next Administration must both adopt a posture that calls for a fully sovereign Mexico and take all steps at its disposal to support that result

title: Move manufacturing from China to Latin America ('re-hemisphering')
proposal: The text recommends using U.S. resources and messaging to shift manufacturing from far-off countries, especially China, to Central and South America.
quote: First, the United States must do everything possible, with both resources and messaging, to shift global manufacturing and industry from more distant points

title: Develop a Western Hemisphere energy policy
proposal: The text recommends working with Mexico, Canada and other countries on a shared energy policy to increase production and reduce reliance on distant fossil fuel sources.
quote: the United States must work with Mexico, Canada, and other countries to develop a hemisphere-focused energy policy

title: Reinstate and expand Trump-era sanctions on Iran
proposal: The text recommends bringing back and expanding the Trump Administration's sanctions on Iran as part of blocking Iran from getting nuclear weapons.
quote: This means, inter alia, reinstituting and expanding Trump Administration sanctions; providing security assistance for regional partners

title: Back Israel's freedom to act against Iran and its proxies
proposal: The text recommends ensuring Israel has the military means and political support to take the steps it decides are needed to defend itself against Iran and groups it backs.
quote: ensuring Israel has both the military means and the political support and flexibility to take what it deems to be appropriate measures to defend itself

title: Encourage Saudi Arabia and others to join the Abraham Accords
proposal: The text recommends encouraging more Arab countries, including Saudi Arabia, to join the Abraham Accords and strengthening ties with Saudi Arabia to limit Chinese influence.
quote: encouraging other Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, to enter the Abraham Accords

title: Defund the Palestinian Authority
proposal: The text recommends ending U.S. funding for the Palestinian Authority.
quote: The Palestinian Authority should be defunded.

title: Build a Middle East security pact (a second 'Quad')
proposal: The text recommends building a Middle East security pact including Israel, Egypt, the Gulf states and possibly India.
quote: it is in the U.S. national interest to build a Middle East security pact that includes Israel, Egypt, the Gulf states, and potentially India

title: Shift aid to Africa from development aid toward private-sector growth
proposal: The text recommends reorienting U.S. development aid in Africa away from stand-alone aid and toward encouraging free markets and U.S. private investment, while keeping emergency relief.
quote: Reorient the focus of U.S. overseas development assistance away from stand-alone humanitarian development aid and toward fostering free market systems in African countries

title: Create a 'digital hygiene' program for African countries
proposal: The text recommends creating a template program African countries can use to protect their communications networks from spying by China and others.
quote: the creation of a template “digital hygiene” program that African countries can access to sanitize and protect their sensitive communications networks

title: Recognize Somaliland as an independent state
proposal: The text recommends that the U.S. formally recognize Somaliland as a state, as a hedge against the weakening U.S. position in Djibouti.
quote: the recognition of Somaliland statehood as a hedge against the U.S.’s deteriorating position in Djibouti

title: Support African military and security forces against terrorism
proposal: The text recommends supporting capable African military and security operations through training, education and security assistance programs.
quote: should support capable African military and security operations through the State Department and other federal agencies responsible for granting foreign military education

title: Focus Africa engagement on designated 'focus countries'
proposal: The text recommends concentrating U.S. resources on African countries the State Department designates as focus countries, while keeping basic contact with others.
quote: After being designated focus countries by the State Department, such nations should receive a full suite of American engagement.

title: Stop promoting abortion and LGBT policies in Africa diplomacy
proposal: The text recommends that U.S. diplomacy in Africa focus on security, economic and human rights matters and stop promoting social policies such as abortion and pro-LGBT initiatives.
quote: The United States should focus on core security, economic, and human rights engagement with African partners and reject the promotion of divisive policies

title: Press NATO allies to meet or exceed 2% of GDP on defense
proposal: The text recommends examining whether NATO members meet the pledge to spend 2 percent of GDP on defense and encouraging them to spend more.
quote: The new Administration will also want to encourage nations to exceed that pledge.

title: Review all U.S.–EU trade arrangements
proposal: The text recommends a full review of trade arrangements between the U.S. and the European Union to make sure U.S. businesses are treated fairly.
quote: The U.S. must undertake a comprehensive review of trade arrangements between the EU and the United States to assure that U.S. businesses are treated fairly

title: Develop trade with the post-Brexit United Kingdom
proposal: The text recommends urgently building up trade with the United Kingdom after its exit from the European Union.
quote: Outside the EU, trade with the post-Brexit U.K. needs urgent development before London slips back into the orbit of the EU.

title: Support a 'Quad-Plus' and a new South Asia strategy
proposal: The text recommends that the State Department encourage other regional powers to join Quad (U.S., India, Japan, Australia) coordination and help lead a revamped South Asia strategy.
quote: The State Department should also encourage the “Quad-Plus” concept that allows other regional powers to participate in Quad coordination

title: Push NATO to adopt an Arctic strategy
proposal: The text recommends that the U.S. treat NATO as partly an Arctic alliance and that NATO adopt a strategy to limit Russia's use of Arctic waters and resources.
quote: NATO must develop and implement an Arctic strategy that recognizes the importance of

title: Expand Navy and Coast Guard fleets, including icebreakers, for the Arctic
proposal: The text recommends that the Navy and Coast Guard keep expanding their fleets, including planned icebreakers, invest in unmanned systems, and consider upgrading the Coast Guard's Barrow station.
quote: It is imperative that the Navy and Coast Guard continue to expand their fleets, including planned icebreaker acquisitions

title: Strengthen economic ties with Greenland
proposal: The text welcomes the U.S. consulate in Nuuk and recommends policies that build closer economic ties between the U.S. and Greenland.
quote: the next Administration should pursue policies that enhance economic ties between the U.S. and Greenland

title: Consider withdrawing from international organizations that lack value
proposal: The text recommends ending automatic support for international organizations and seriously considering leaving those that no longer help U.S. interests or rely heavily on U.S. money.
quote: Serious consideration should also be given to withdrawal from organizations that no longer have value, quietly undermine U.S. interests or goals

title: Do a cost-benefit review of U.S. membership in all international organizations
proposal: The text recommends that the Secretary of State review the costs and benefits of U.S. participation in every international organization, with a view to withholding funds where abuses occur.
quote: The next Administration should direct the Secretary of State to initiate a comprehensive cost-benefit analysis of U.S. participation in all international organizations.

title: Use a sovereignty and 'authentic human rights' test for international posts
proposal: The text recommends promoting a strict, text-based reading of treaties and using respect for sovereignty and human rights as a test in personnel decisions and elections at international organizations.
quote: including by making respect for sovereignty and authentic human rights a litmus test of personnel decisions and elections processes within international organizations

title: Base human rights policy on the Commission on Unalienable Rights report
proposal: The text recommends using the report of the U.S. Commission on Unalienable Rights as the basis for State Department changes, and halting initiatives that promote controversial policies.
quote: should be the basis for both structural and policy changes throughout the State Department

title: Align foreign policy with the Geneva Consensus Declaration
proposal: The text recommends aligning U.S. foreign policy efforts started or expanded under Obama and Biden with the Geneva Consensus Declaration on women's health and the family.
quote: must be aligned with the Geneva Consensus Declaration and the work of the U.S. Commission on Unalienable Human Rights

title: Do not fund or promote abortion in international programs
proposal: The text recommends that the U.S. not promote or fund abortion through international programs or multilateral groups, and build a coalition of like-minded nations on this.
quote: The U.S. government should not and cannot promote or fund abortion in

title: Restrict U.S. funding to the World Health Organization
proposal: The text recommends greater limits on federal money to the WHO and other international health groups until they change their policies.
quote: the supply of federal dollars to the WHO and other health-focused international organizations pending adjustment of their policies.

title: Draft a full reorganization plan for the State Department
proposal: The text recommends developing a complete reorganization of the department to cut overhead and redundancy, including deciding which offices can be closed with or without Congress.
quote: The next Administration should develop a complete hypothetical reorganization of the department

title: Make the USAID chief a Director of Foreign Assistance over all aid
proposal: The text recommends giving the USAID administrator the added role of Director of Foreign Assistance, at Deputy Secretary rank, to oversee all U.S. foreign aid.
quote: should be authorized to take on the additional role of Director of Foreign Assistance with the rank of Deputy Secretary and oversee all foreign assistance

title: Consolidate foreign aid programs spread across agencies
proposal: The text recommends checking whether the many separate sources of foreign aid serve the national interest and, if not, planning to combine those authorities.
quote: develop a plan to consolidate foreign assistance authorities

title: Restore and consolidate U.S. international broadcasting
proposal: The text recommends rebuilding U.S. international broadcasting, combining broadcasting resources, and refocusing content on pro-freedom messaging.
quote: restoring its international broadcasting infrastructure as part of the broader U.S. foreign policy framework, consolidating broadcasting resources

title: Seek enforceable international rules for cyberspace
proposal: The text recommends that the State Department work with allies on a framework of enforceable rules for behavior in cyberspace, going beyond voluntary U.N. norms.
quote: The State Department should work with allies to establish a clear framework of enforceable norms for actions in cyberspace

title: Help the military take offensive action in cyberspace
proposal: The text recommends that the State Department assist the Department of Defense in going "on offence" against cyber adversaries rather than relying on deterrence alone.
quote: The State Department should also assist the Department of Defense to go “on offence” against adversaries.
